# Letter of Agreement between Paris ACC and Bordeaux ACC

Creation 2026/06 - Effective 2606

## Distribution and Scope

This Letter of Agreement (LoA) outlines the agreements between Paris ACC and Bordeaux ACC (the French vACC for the provision of air traffic services).

## Exclusion of Liability

> The procedures outlined in this Letter of Agreement (LoA) are **exclusively intended for use within the VATSIM Network** and should never be implemented in real-world scenarios.
{.is-warning}

The information contained in this document is provided without any warranties. French vACC disclaims any responsibility or liability, whether direct or indirect, concerning the accuracy, currency, or quality of the information, as well as any consequences resulting from its utilisation. 

Several procedures have been adapted or developed based on content published within the Aeronautical Information Services (AIS) of both nations. This document does not replace official procedures, and any procedures similar to or influenced by online content are formulated under the Limited License granted by the two AISs.

# Section 1 - General

This Letter of Agreement outlines the coordination procedures between Paris ACC (French vACC) and Bordeaux ACC (French vACC) for providing air traffic services (ATS) to General Air Traffic (IFR). 

These procedures supplement those outlined in ICAO, VATSIM Regulations, inter-Division or inter-virtual air traffic service provider agreements, and/or national documents. If a translated version exists in another language, the English version shall take precedence in case of any interpretation discrepancies.

# Section 3 - Procedures for coordination
## General Conditions for Acceptance of Flights

1. Coordination of flights shall take place using the coordination point (COP) and in accordance with the appropriate levels specified for the relevant route.
1. Flights shall be considered to be maintaining the coordinated flight level at the transfer of control point unless climb or descent conditions have been clearly stated by use of coordination
1. If the accepting ATS unit cannot accept a flight offered in accordance with the conditions specified above, it shall clearly indicate its inability and specify the conditions under which it will accept the flight.
1. For any proposed deviation from the conditions specified in this LoA (e.g. COP, route or level), the transferring unit shall initiate an Approval Request using the appropriate software tool.
1. The accepting ATS unit shall accept the electronic transfer of the aircraft upon establishing communications with the transferred aircraft. The Accepting Unit shall notify the transferring Unit if communication with the aircraft is not established as expected.

## ATS Routes, Coordination Points and Level Allocation

Available ATS routes, COPs to be used, and level allocation to be applied are described in the tables below.

Upon transfer, IFR aircraft are to conform to ICAO standard cruising levels (or agreed levels if these differ), except as outlined below, and to incorporate Reduced Vertical Separation Minima (RVSM) and to follow the direction of ATS routes as published in the relevant AIP.

Due to the nature of traffic flow over France, ICAO standard cruising levels are not applicable. Instead, the North-South rule applies when no level parity is defined on an ATS route, or when traffic is not following an ATS route. LMH to FL410, traffic with a general heading between 271° and 089° shall cruise at an even flight level. Traffic with a general heading between 090° and 270° shall cruise at an odd flight level. 

Should a parity change be needed, it shall be performed by the sending unit before the border or coordinated point of transfer to the receiving unit.

> All flights are **released to turn along its trajectory by 45° maximum**, by the next sector. The giving sector remains the only one responsible for the separation within its area.
{.is-info}

### LFPO Group, LFPG Group, LFOB Group Departures

Flights departing from Orly Group, CDG Group, and Beauvais Group are strategically separated when established on adjacent SIDs. Paris ACC can clear departures to the following waypoints without prior coordination: AGOPA, ERIXU, and LATRA. Any direct routes beyond these must be coordinated.

_Departure Trajectories_:

- ARKIP DCT ARNAV DCT LMG are spaced by 10NM or more from EDOXA-ERIXU-ETAMO and LALUX-LATRA-LAMUT

_Departure Planning_:

- ARKIP DCT ARNAV DCT LMG is considred equal to the following departure: ADADA DCT AGOPA DCT ARKIP DCT ARMAL DCT ARTAX

**Handover Communication**

If different groups depart from Roissy and Beauvais on separate SIDs, Paris ACC will do its best to hand over the aircraft simultaneously. The same applies to the Orly departure group. In all cases, especially for departures from LFPG and LFOB, the handover of DODG communication to the P sector must not occur before the line indicated by the TABOV-RESMI-TEPRI route (see below figure).

![tabov-resmi-tepri.png](/doc-atc/lfbb/tabov-resmi-tepri.png)

If flights reach FL260 before hitting this limit (see Figure 2), DODG will try to get a higher FL from the UZ sector and will file this level in CoFrance. Since the level is being filled, coordination with DODG & P is not required.

#### Distinction

|Departure Group|Sector|Maximum Flight Level|Conditions|
|:--------------:|:------------------------:|:--------:|
| Roissy and Beauvais | DODG | FL260 | RFL if lower

#### Lateral and vertical release

Except for special conditions, DODG sends those flights not conflictual with the R25C area and separated from flights with destination LMH sector, as well as flights with destination DODG on the AMODO-RESMI axis. 

_Special Conditions_:

- North of TABOV-RESMI-TEPRI, P sector has no release.
- South of TABOV-RESMI-TEPRI, the release applies from the moment of handover communication in the following conditions: free to turn and climb in DODG limits. P doesn’t deliver trajectory alternation as in might result in a potential conflict with awaiting aircraft not yet on his frequency.

#### Sequencing

Suppose multiple aircraft are succeeding on the same SID. DODG hands over the flights in sequence. If the P sector must maintain a departure from Paris TMA at FL250, DODG must be informed. The latter is in charge of separation for the AGOPA ERIXU LATRA axis.

### Exit via SIQLE

AVLON-OKEPI-SIQLE-LAKOB axis is exclusively reserved for LFLA, LFOK, LFQA, LFQB departures. Those flights are sent at FL260. Paris ACC ensures their compatibility with the PIBAT-MOU-ENUPA trajectory.

### ARKIP DCT ARNAV DCT LMG: during military activity of TRA10 A, B, C, R25

In case of conflict with TRA 10 A, B, C, R25C, a rerouting requiring a modification of the Route (in the FPL) will be implemented after coordination.

## Flights from Bordeaux ACC to Paris ACC

POI-PEPAX-NIMER, ADABI-BOKNO-DEVRO, and TUDRA-BEVOL-AMB are parallel at 10 nm until the handover control waypoint, and thereafter diverge.

For flights delivered simultaneously on those trajectories, the transfer of radar control might be performed without prior coordination as long as the following conditions are met:

1. Flights are on the planned trajectory, at the latest at the POI, ADABI, TUDRA
2. Before the handover, the giving sector notifies the trajectory to follow for each flight by indicating at least the first 2 report points for the next sector:
3. POI: PEPAX-NIMER-KEPER
3.1 ADABI: BOKNO-DEVRO-VANAD
3.2 TUDRA: BEVOL-AMB-DOMOD
3.3 At the time of the handover, a specific radar monitoring should confirm that these flights are well established on the notified trajectory

### AMB compatibility

Paris ACC oversees the compatibility of South-North traffic at AMB, following POI-AMB (B19) and LMG-AMB (A34/R10).

### PEPAX Trajectory

Exclusively reserved for LFPG and associated. Flights are handover FL300 steady at PEPAX at the latest. R2 sector sequence flights by ensuring a-10-mile distance between 2 successive arrivals. 

**FL290 and FL270** can be used by Bordeaux ACC as alternate FLs after coordination with Paris ACC. At OG's initiative, those levels can be used as well, notably in the case of simultaneous arrivals on PEPAX and BOKNO at FL300.
FL260 and FL280 are systematically coordinated.

### BEVOL Trajectory

Flights passing through BEVOL are:
- Either flying to LFPO, LFPV, LFPN and handed over FL280 max at BEVOL, sequenced at 10 miles.  If sequencing is impossible, Bordeaux is invited to use FL260 as an alternate FL after coordination with OG. 
- Or flying to LFPM, LFOC, LFOJ, LFOZ, LFAI and delivering FL200 steady at BEVOL.

> For Orly Group, Bordeaux Coordination point is AMB.
{.is-info}

### BOKNO Trajectory

Flights with destinations: LFOE, LFOH, LFOP, LFRG, LFOB, LFPT, LFRK, LFAQ are delivered to OG, FL300 max, on the ADABI-BOKNO trajectory.
Flights departing LFBL are handed over at FL260 max to BOKNO.

### ENUPA Trajectory

Flights planning route via ENUPA are defined in the RAD.

●	**Flights from Bordeaux to Paris ACC:**

Those flights are exchanged from the P1 sector to the LMH sector, at FL220 max, except for flights with LFOK/QA/QB/LA/GJ/SD destinations, which are handed over at FL200, steady at the crossing of LAKOB-LERGA axis (KUKOR), at the latest to the SDS sector. The latter ensures the continuous descent to avoid the LMH sector.  

For TRA24 activity, ENUPA-MOU-PIBAT-DJL is unusable. In this case, on the initiative of Paris ACC and after coordination, the LMH sector can refuse a flight in Paris UIR.

●	**Flights from Paris ACC to Bordeaux ACC:**

Those flights are handed over to P sector climbing or steady to FL230 max.

### LFBI and LFLX Departures via AMB

LFBI and LFLX departures are coordinated and handed over by Poitiers APP (or Bordeaux when Poitiers is closed) to the OT sector to FL140 max. If FL120 cannot be reached at the FIR limit, coordination must be performed between Poitiers Approach and Seine Approach.

### LFOT South Departures

Seine APP coordinates LFOT South Departure to Poitiers APP (or Bordeaux when Poitiers APP is closed) to FL110 maximum to OMARI. 
If RFL>FL145, Poitiers coordinates and hands over the flight to LM (Bordeaux).
South departure must not enter the Paris OT sector; in case of a high rate of climb, Seine APP will coordinate with the OT sector.

### LFOT South Arrivals

LM sector (Bordeaux) coordinates and hands over LFOT arrivals to Poitiers APP. After coordination between Poitiers APP and Seine APP, with 5 min advance notice, LFOT arrivals are sent by Poitiers APP to Seine on course OMARI or OT802 at FL110 max. 

> South arrivals must not enter the OT sector.
{.is-info}

### LFJR (Angers) Arrivals via POI-GINON

Those flights are handed over to Poitiers Approach at FL140 maximum, with the following profile: LM - BI - NB and avoid the Paris’ RT sector.

### LFBK (Montluçon) Departures via MOU

Limoges Approach coordinates and directly hands over flights to Paris to FL140 max, avoiding the Bordeaux LM sector.

### Saint Yan Group Arrivals

Saint Yan (LFLN) and its associated arrivals via LEMIN, below FL145, are processed directly between Limoges Approach and Clermont-Ferrand Approach.

### Special procedures

LFRM arrivals via AMB are handed over at FL190 max.

Bordeaux ACC (LM) sends LFOQ arrivals to Paris ACC at FL160 max.

LFBI and LFLX departures are coordinated and handed over to Paris ACC by Poitiers Approach at FL140 max. Those flights avoid LM.

### LFLC and LFLV Arrivals via RESMI-KOTAP-KETEX-KOTIS and TRARE-ATRID (A3)

These flights connect to the FIR network at FL190 maximum.
Procedure according to RFL:

- RFL lower than FL265: those flights avoid Bordeaux.
- RFL higher than FL265: after coordination, Bordeaux P1 sector hands over those flights to DODG sector at FL270 steady or in descent to FL270.

## VFR

LFFF (FIR) does not accept VFR flights above FL115.
LFBB does not accept VFR flights in UIR, either at FL195 or at FL145.

# Section 4 - ATS Surveillance-Based Co-ordination Procedures
## Transfer of Aircraft Identification

- Transfer of aircraft identification between Bordeaux ACC and Paris ACC is usually performed by transfer of the aircraft tag.
- When discrete SSR codes are used for transfer of identification, they shall be assigned in accordance with ORCAM or other VATSIM network-defined ranges.
- Any change of the SSR code by the accepting ATS Unit may only take place after the transfer of the control point.
- The accepting ATS Unit shall be notified of any observed irregularity in the operation of SSR transponders.

## Radar Co-ordination Procedures
### General

Transfer of radar identification and radar control between Paris ACC and Bordeaux ACC will be subject to the serviceability of the equipment used by controllers and to the VATSIM data network being sufficient for the necessary information exchange. Additionally, two-way communication between the two facilities should be possible.

If it becomes necessary to reduce or suspend transfers of control, a 5-minute prior notification shall be observed, except in emergencies.

### Transfer of Radar Control

Transfer of radar control may be performed, after prior coordination, provided the minimum separation between the aircraft does not fall below 5 NM.

### 4.2.3	Silent Transfer of Control (Silent Handover)

Transfer of control may take place by means of a Silent Handover, provided that:

●	The aircraft concerned are following the _same route_, they are spaced by a minimum of 10 NM, constant or increasing.
●	The receiving controller is informed – by means of XFL electronic coordination or otherwise – of any level restriction other than an aircraft’s requested flight level or those covered by Standing Agreement before transfer of communications.

## Separation Minima
### Separation between COPs

Traffic via COPs spaced less than 10 NM apart are to be considered the same for Longitudinal Separation. If there is any doubt regarding lateral separation, then vertical separation must be provided.

### Radar Separation

The following radar separation minima are to be applied:

●	Paris ACC: 	**5 NM**
●	Bordeaux ACC: 	**5 NM**

Where the radar separation minima at the boundary differ, the greater minima of the relevant units shall be applied to all transfers.
